messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a controlled dry-run to compare scale-up behavior between two kernel stacks and priming strategies. Goal: apples-to-apples on scale-up latency, cold start work, and burst-credit usage. Running at 50qps -> 400 concurrent tokens across a 4-GPU dedicated pool. Dry-run starts 14:00 PT.

mar ia: Plan attached inline (short): 1) synthetic steady ramp (0->50qps over 90s), 2) replay harness (production traces, same ramp), 3) toggles: KV warm vs KV cold, batching heuristics default vs aggressive, kernel: cuda-v2 vs kernel-x.

tim: nice. how are you measuring "scale-up time" exactly? wall-clock from first request queued to all requested replicas ready?

maria: scale-up time = from first exceed-threshold event (node-level OOM or queue-latency crossover) to observed p95 return to baseline (within 10%). also capture scheduler events and container create times.

vivaan: can we also capture kernel-selection decisions? need to know which kernel each instance selected at each seq length. otherwise apples-to-apples fails.

maria: yes — adding profiler hook to log kernel_id per invocation + batch shape histogram. will export as compact CSV: timestamp,kernel,batch_shape,seq_len,latency_ms.

alyssa: add in KV cache warmup metric: earliest token served from cache vs fallback. we saw big cold-start regressions previously.

jorge: for replay harness, make sure we pin same seed & distribution. also disable autoscaler growth smoothing for this run so we see raw response.

maria: run config (pasted):

```
POOL=dedicated-gpu-4
RAMP_SECONDS=90
TARGET_QPS=50
SEQUENCE_LENGTH=512
BATCH_POLICY=aggressive|default
KV_PRIMING=true|false
KERNELS=["cuda-v2","kernel-x"]
REPLAY_SEED=2026-03-18
CAPTURE=[scheduler_events,container_create,kv_hit, kernel_id, batch_hist]
```

maria: deploy-bot will do the canary deploy and log the container image hash. will tag runs with run_id.

deploy-bot: canary deploy triggered — run_id=run-1935001111. images: cuda-v2@sha256:aa3, kernel-x@sha256:bb7. Rolling out to test pool.

tim: reminder: include the profiler flame sample at 2x and 10x congestion points. we need to see where kernel-x stalls on memcpy or sync.

vivaan: initial dry-run observations (quick summary):
- synthetic + KV cold: kernel-x scale-up faster (container create ~18s vs 27s) but p95 spikes larger (kernel-x p95=1200ms vs cuda-v2 p95=820ms).
- KV warm drastically reduces initial p95 on both (median ~300ms).
- aggressive batching reduces GPU utilization variance but increased tail by ~12% at high concurrency.

alyssa: can you paste the mini trace where we saw the p95 spike?

vivaan: dropping snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T21:12:33Z,request_id=abc123,kernel=kernel-x,batch_shape=[1,48,1],seq=512,latency=1250ms,kv_hit=false
2026-03-18T21:12:34Z,request_id=abc124,kernel=kernel-x,batch_shape=[1,64,1],seq=512,latency=1189ms,kv_hit=false
```

jorge: that batch shape looks weird — lots of stragglers producing tiny batches. could be our batching heuristic mis-evaluating timeouts.

maria: action items from dry-run: 
- Add guard to avoid batch shapes with dominant small-first-dim when >80% of active tokens are long-seq.
- Tune batching timeout from 5ms -> 3ms in aggressive mode and re-run.
- Add KV priming warmup script to pre-populate likely prefixes for replay harness.
- Collect full profiler + perf counters for next run.

sre-bot: note: this test will consume burst credits for the dedicated pool. estimate ~18 minutes of burst at current ramp, confirm approval.

alyssa: approve — go ahead. we want the data to validate autoscaler tweak. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. re-run scheduled in 10m with the above tweaks. I'll paste final results after the complete harness (will include csv and small notebook link).

maria: final note — if kernel-x continues to show lower scale-up latency but worse tails, we should consider hybrid routing: prefer kernel-x for predictable short seqs and cuda-v2 for long-seq critical paths. need more data but this will guide rollout policies.

maria: end of thread (will attach artifacts).
